Headteacher's Welcome
As a headteacher, I strongly believe that creating a warm and welcoming environment is essential for children to learn and develop. I encourage open communication between myself, my staff, our pupils, and their families. We respect and value each individual's opinion and encourage them to express it openly.
At our school, we have an open-door policy which allows our pupils to easily talk about their ideas or concerns ideas with us. We strive to create a place where everyone feels valued and respected while also providing the resources for our children to succeed in their studies.
We continuously strive to find engaging and innovative ways to help all our children learn, develop and achieve highly as individuals. We build close partnerships with families and celebrate success together.
This website aims to give you a taster of the school, as well as providing up to date information for parents, carers, children and the wider community. We hope that you enjoy your visit to our website, and that you find the information you are looking for. Please feel free to contact the school direct with any queries you may have.
We welcome visits to the school, and look forward to showing visitors the hardworking and purposeful atmosphere that permeates throughout our school.
Mrs Nina Will Headteacher​​

What is expected of Governors?
How often are the Governing Body Meetings?
The full Governing Body usually meets twice, once each term and is attended by the Clerk to the Governors (Lucia Perdoni).
What happens?
The agenda will include:
Sometimes a meeting will contain items of a confidential nature. These will be put in Part 2 of the agenda and minutes of the meeting, and Governors are expected to maintain confidentiality.
Papers relating to items on the agenda are circulated a week before the meeting. Governors are expected to read these beforehand.
Making decisions on issues affecting the schools
Panels
All Governors need to become members of a panel. These panels meet very occasionally as the need arises. These are set up permanently but meet only as required to deal with various aspects.
Responsibilities of the Governing Body
To act as a corporate body
To approve the budget plan annually
Delegating work to committees
A Governing Body can fulfil some of its responsibilities through committees. At Stag Lane Primary School we have the following committees which meet once a term, apart from the resource committee which meets more often

Modern Foreign Languages - French
MFL Curriculum Our curriculum coverage
At Stag Lane we have a serve a rich diverse community, with many languages spoken. As the majority of our children are bilingual, we aim to nurture their language accusation skills to learn a new language. Our teaching encourage curiosity, inspiration and a love of languages through culture days.
We provide a broad and balanced French curriculum with a clear and comprehensive scheme of work in line with the National Curriculum expectations. We Offer children opportunities to develop a range of social and teamwork skills, through developing students’ oracy, literacy, comprehension and cultural understanding. Our lessons ensure children can use their language skills in real life situations.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Music curriculum Intent statement:
The intent of our Music curriculum is to deliver a curriculum which is accessible to all and that will maximise the development of every child’s ability and academic achievement in the area of Music. Stag Lane has identified key intentions that drive our music curriculum. Our music curriculum intentions are: 1) To provide an interesting well-balanced Music curriculum which develops the students’ knowledge and musicality through the interrelated activities of performing, composing, appraising and listening. 2) To provide students with opportunities to learn instruments.3) To develop our children’s confidence and wellbeing through Musical activities and 4) To inspire our pupils to love Music and take a pride in their achievements, leading to lifelong appreciation & enjoyment of the Arts.

Afterschool Clubs at Stag Lane
Welcome to our afterschool clubs page. Here you will find all you need to know about the clubs we run as a school and also other companies who run clubs with us.
At Stag Lane we are very fortunate to be able to offer a wide selection of clubs to our children in Years Reception to Year 6 and make use of the available space we have including the field, playground and halls.
Some of these clubs are offered free and teachers offer to do these clubs in their spare time. Some of the clubs offered do carry a small fee to cover expenses. There is also a Wrap around care club available for after school everyday up until 18:00pm.
Clubs get booked up very quickly so please make sure you look out for our clubs email in September (Autumn Term), end of December (Spring Clubs) and end of March (Summer Clubs).

A message from the Chair of the Full Governing Board
"My role as Chair is to work with the School in setting a strategic direction through championing vision, ethos, and strategy of Stag Lane primary school. Governance has never been more critical to the education of all children, and at Stag Lane Primary School I am proud to say we are excellent at this.
Along the way, we have had many challenges but none so unique as the 2020 pandemic and School amalgamation which has gone well, to do this we at Stag lane have an excellent team of governors who work with the school to deliver oversight as a critical friend to the school.
Every time I step into school, I am impressed by the dedication and the enthusiasm that is infectious to anyone involved at our school.
The end results are not bad either, which is better educated future citizens of the world."
Antoinette Watt, FGB Chair
The Governing Body
Our Governing Body is made up of representatives of the Local Authority, parents, teachers, staff and members of the local community. The Governing Body's role is to make many decisions about the way our school serves our children and their parents. Here are our Governors 2024-2025.
